settings.about: Dr. Laurenie Louissaint is double board-certified in Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation and Sports Medicine. Her practice centers on sports medicine and interventional spine care, informed by her own path from Division I athlete and athletic trainer at Florida International University to physician and national-team doctor. She serves as Assistant Professor of Sports Medicine at SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University and as Head Team Physician for the Haiti Women’s National Team through the Haitian Football Federation.
settings.hero_intro: Double board-certified in Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation and Sports Medicine, Dr. Louissaint primarily practices sports medicine and interventional spine care. As an Assistant Professor at SUNY Downstate and Head Team Physician for the Haiti Women’s National Team, she brings advanced clinical training and an athlete’s perspective to helping patients recover, perform, and remain active.

entries.title: Beyond the “Like”: A Framework for Social Media Professionalism as a Physician
entries.summary: A co-authored framework for physicians navigating professional identity, patient boundaries, advocacy, and evidence-based communication online.
entries.body: Published in Family Doctor, A Journal of the New York State Academy of Family Physicians, Spring 2026, Volume 14, Number 4. Co-authored with Christine S. Persaud, MD, MBA; Ahmed Ashai, MD; and Stephen Hongach, DO, MS.

entries.title: Integrative Medicine as It Relates to Musculoskeletal Pain
entries.summary: A clinical review of evidence-informed integrative approaches to musculoskeletal pain, including acupuncture, movement-based therapies, and mind-body interventions.
entries.body: Published as View One in “Two Views: Integrative Medicine and the Musculoskeletal System” in Family Doctor, A Journal of the New York State Academy of Family Physicians, Summer 2025, Volume 14, Number 1. Co-authored with Christine Persaud, MD, MBA, FAAFP, FAMSSM; Sejal Khan, DO, MS; and Patrick Cleary, DO.

entries.title: Joined the Haiti Women’s National Team as Head Team Physician
entries.summary: Joined the Haitian Football Federation as Head Team Physician for the Haiti Women’s National Team.
entries.body: In this role, Dr. Louissaint supports the women’s national team with physician leadership, athlete health oversight, injury-prevention planning, and coordinated sports medicine care.

entries.title: Rehabilitation Medicine Missions in Namibia
entries.summary: Two clinical-service trips supporting rehabilitation care and hands-on medical education in Windhoek, Namibia.
entries.body: Dr. Louissaint traveled to Namibia twice with rehabilitation medicine colleagues, returning in 2024 after an earlier service mission. The teams treated high volumes of patients, supported image-guided and peripheral joint procedures, and worked alongside local clinicians to expand sustainable pain and rehabilitation care.

entries.title: Medical and Rehabilitation Service in Haiti
entries.summary: Mission-based medical and rehabilitation service connected to Haiti after the 2010 earthquake.
entries.body: After the 2010 earthquake, Dr. Louissaint volunteered in Haiti through Project Medishare and later returned with the Haiti Rehab Project. The experiences connected her family’s Haitian roots with a long-term commitment to medicine, rehabilitation, and service in communities with limited access to care.

entries.title: Joined SUNY Downstate in Academic Sports Medicine
entries.summary: Joined the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery and Rehabilitation Medicine with a focus on sports medicine and pain management.
entries.body: Dr. Louissaint serves as Assistant Professor of Sports Medicine at SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University and contributes to Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation resident education.

entries.title: Sports Medicine & Interventional Spine Fellowship
entries.summary: Advanced fellowship training at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai from August 2023 through July 2024.
entries.body: Following residency in Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Dr. Louissaint completed fellowship training in Sports Medicine and Interventional Spine at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai from August 2023 through July 2024.

entries.title: Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation Residency
entries.summary: Completed Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation residency at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai from July 2020 through July 2023.
entries.body: Her residency training from July 2020 through July 2023 developed a broad foundation in rehabilitation medicine, function, musculoskeletal care, and the non-operative treatment of active patients.

entries.title: Doctor of Medicine
entries.summary: Earned her medical degree from Ross University School of Medicine.
entries.body: Dr. Louissaint studied medicine at Ross University School of Medicine from 2014 through 2018. A former Division I athlete and athletic trainer at Florida International University, she brought an established foundation in movement, performance, and rehabilitation to her medical training.

entries.title: A Commitment to Medicine and Service
entries.summary: The 2010 earthquake in Haiti became a defining catalyst in Dr. Louissaint’s decision to pursue medicine.
entries.body: After the earthquake devastated Haiti, where her parents were raised, she sought ways to support the response. The experience reinforced her determination to pursue a medical degree and expand the care she could provide.

entries.title: Appointed to SUNY Downstate’s Orthopaedic Department
entries.summary: Dr. Louissaint announced her role in Brooklyn specializing in sports medicine and pain management.
entries.body: The academic appointment brings together clinical care, medical education, and Dr. Louissaint’s experience in sports medicine, physiatry, and pain management.

entries.title: Ross University Alumni Profile: “It Only Takes One”
entries.summary: A profile tracing the journey from Division I athlete and athletic trainer to physician.
entries.body: Ross University School of Medicine profiled Dr. Louissaint’s path, family influences, connection to Haiti, medical education, and commitment to breaking barriers.
